# altitude — the coarse-observer picture on its own terms: an identity, a continuous altitude, the frontier read off the logits, the model as a null, and what a violation does to the forecast

**Up**: [../README.md](../README.md) (logit_reading) · **Files**: [FILES.md](FILES.md) ·
**Tables**: [results/tables.md](results/tables.md) (every number below and more) ·
**Figures**: `figs/*.png` (regenerated by `analyze.py`; PNGs are gitignored under `experiments/`)
**Date**: 2026-09-16 · **Status**: all five questions run, plus two CPU addenda (the residual's
location per checkpoint; what the post-violation forecast moves toward).
**Prompt**: the conversation reading [`../README.md`](../README.md) after it merged (PR #114): the
correspondence between the logits and a family of coarse Bayesian observers looked like it might be
the piece a learner needs to judge new representations with its current ones, and the question was
what the node actually establishes and what to run next. Jasper's steer was to run the round so it
stands on its own, in the node's own terms, rather than aligned to any other line in the repo.
**Attribution**: the five questions, the `CE − H(q)` derivation and the "closest rung, not on the
rung" caution are the orchestrator's; the on-its-own-terms framing and the collapsed-distribution
question (§What this does not establish) are Jasper's; the build, every gate, the feature-level
candidate construction in Q3, and the correction to the residual-shape reading in Q2 are the
implementer's (one Opus session).

## Goal

The parent node fit a next-token model's logits to a one-parameter family of exact Bayesian
predictors — *observer k* knows the bottom `k` of the grammar's six levels and treats everything
above as i.i.d. — and found the best-fit `k` climbs one rung at a time, while the logits stay
calibrated to their own loss throughout. Its Part 2 read a grammar violation from the model's
state and output. Five questions about that picture, each answerable exactly on this substrate:

1. Is "the logits predict their own loss" a finding or an identity, and is the discrete rung the
   right altitude?
2. Can the model locate its own frontier — the level it is learning and where in the stream that
   level's news lives — from its logits alone?
3. Used as a null hypothesis, does the model's predictive score candidate next-level units, and
   at which levels?
4. The two controls Part 2 was missing: an exact observer's running surprisal in the tonic
   design, and a noise-aware observer at the model's own altitude in the entropy-direction design.
5. Does a model trained on the corruption the noise-aware observer models join that observer's
   family, and does its post-violation entropy change sign?

Same substrate as the parent throughout (`v16 s2 L6 m4`, `generate_rules_distinct(seed=0)`,
`8L/8H/256D`, the 13-checkpoint `traj_a1_s42` trajectory with Dirichlet(1) synonym weights, the
`a1` and `swap65k` stimuli). Q1–Q3 are CPU passes over the per-checkpoint `*_calibration.npz`
arrays the parent already wrote (all 13 checkpoints share the same 4096 held-out windows and the
same model-independent observer predictives). New GPU time: one 55-minute trajectory (Q5) and
about 40 minutes of short sweeps.

## Instrument additions

- **A continuous altitude.** `argmin_k mean KL(p_k‖q)` is replaced by a fit over the convex family
  `p_κ = (1−λ) p_k + λ p_{k+1}`, `κ = k + λ`, on a 0.05 grid. Log-linear interpolation is reported
  and rejected: supports are nested, so the geometric mean collapses to `supp p_{k+1}` for any
  `λ > 0` and is worse than convex at every checkpoint. Two two-parameter references say whether a
  one-parameter altitude is the right shape: `(k, ε)` uniform-smoothed observers and `(κ, α)`
  tempered convex observers.
- **The ε-noise family as a second ladder.** `flat_predictive(..., noise_eps=ε)` for every `k`,
  cached once per window set; a checkpoint is fit against 14 observers (clean and ε, `k = 0…6`).
- **What the post-token forecast moves toward.** On the same-prefix pairs of the parent's
  [`phasic.py`](../phasic.py), rebuilt exactly on CPU, `KL(q_next ‖ p_{k,next})` for every
  observer in both families, after the violating token and after its legal twin.

## Q1 — the identity, the temperature, and a continuous altitude

**`CE − H(q)` is `⟨q − p, z⟩`, the derivative of `CE(p, softmax(αz))` at `α = 1`.** Pointwise, at
every checkpoint, max |difference| over 262,144 predictions is 1.4e−07 to 4.5e−07 (the float32
logit-storage floor). Two consequences follow analytically and check numerically: the gap is
increasing in `α` (its derivative is `Var_{q_α}(z) ≥ 0`), and its root is exactly the temperature
that minimises `KL(p_L‖q_α)`. So a softmax with a free logit scale zeroes the gap by construction
once trained, in every context class it can scale separately.

| step | `CE − H(q)` | `α*` (the scale that zeroes it) | `KL(p_L‖q)` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | +0.146 | none for `α ≥ 0` | 1.665 |
| 250 | −0.060 | 1.087 | 0.541 |
| 500 | −0.022 | 1.031 | 0.365 |
| 2 000 | −0.006 | 1.011 | 0.202 |
| 8 000 | −0.000 | 1.000 | 0.085 |
| 16 000 | −0.001 | 1.002 | 0.054 |
| 24 000 | −0.005 | 1.010 | 0.041 |
| 64 000 | −0.004 | 1.008 | 0.017 |

At 64k the per-class `α*` is 1.007–1.016 across window-position buckets, 0.963–1.013 across token
levels and 0.992–1.122 across entropy deciles, with mean per-class gaps of −0.015 to +0.013. The
step-250 gap is negative: the temperature lags the content. Rescaling the 64k logits by `α` from
0.6 to 2.0 sweeps the gap from −0.206 to +0.512 and the ECE from 0.088 to 0.003 (at `α ≈ 1`) to
0.136, while `best_k` stays 5 for every `α` in `[0.6, 1.5]` and flips to 6 only at `α = 2`. The
parent's `R²(CE ~ H(q)) = 0.99` reduces to the same condition as a second moment,
`≈ 1 − var(gap)/var(CE)`; it is 0.99 within window-position classes, 0.97 → 0.62 from token level 0
to 6, and 0.00–0.63 within entropy deciles, so the pooled number is mostly across-class variation
in `H(q)`.

> **"The logits predict their own loss" is the temperature-direction stationarity condition of
> the loss, satisfied in every class the model can scale. It says nothing about the model's
> knowledge of itself. What carries content is which distribution the logits are.**

**The altitude.** The convex fit is smooth and monotone where the argmin is a staircase (it sticks
at 2 for three checkpoints, then jumps). Neither the `(k, ε)` floor (best `ε = 0` from 16k on) nor
a temperature on top of `p_κ` (best `α → 1.00` at convergence) buys anything, so the one-parameter
convex family is the right shape.

| step | `best_k` | `KL(p_k‖q)` | **`κ*`** | **`KL(p_κ*‖q)`** | `KL(p_L‖q)` | **`KL(p_κ*‖q)` / `KL(p_L‖q)`** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0.187 | 0.00 | 0.187 | 1.665 | 0.11 |
| 250 | 1 | 0.143 | 1.30 | 0.117 | 0.541 | 0.22 |
| 1 000 | 2 | 0.082 | 2.20 | 0.077 | 0.272 | 0.28 |
| 2 000 | 2 | 0.111 | 2.55 | 0.073 | 0.202 | 0.36 |
| 4 000 | 3 | 0.080 | 2.85 | 0.071 | 0.130 | 0.55 |
| 8 000 | 4 | 0.062 | 3.70 | 0.052 | 0.085 | 0.61 |
| 16 000 | 4 | 0.042 | 4.40 | 0.038 | 0.054 | 0.70 |
| 24 000 | 5 | 0.037 | 4.55 | 0.029 | 0.041 | 0.70 |
| 48 000 | 5 | 0.019 | 4.80 | 0.018 | 0.023 | 0.77 |
| 64 000 | 5 | 0.015 | 4.90 | 0.014 | 0.017 | 0.81 |

The last column is the parent's "near-exact posterior of a coarse observer" turned into a trend:
the best member of the family is 9× closer to the logits than the truth is at step 250 and 1.2×
closer at 64k. The per-position `κ` (argmin per prediction) tracks `κ*` but saturates lower (4.12
at 64k) with a broad histogram over `[2, 6]`, the continuous form of the `best_k` spread the parent
flags.

## Q2 — the frontier from the logits, and where the residual lives

**A. The depth-k boundary, recovered from the entropy of `q` alone.** Under observer `k` the
predictive returns to the depth-k marginal at every depth-k boundary, so the per-position entropy
should carry a period of `s^k`. Detector: correlate each window's entropy profile against the
model-independent template `E[H(p_k) | leaf level]` over the `s^k` candidate offsets (a plain
argmax-of-offset-profile detector agrees to within 0.01–0.07). Accuracy = P(recovered offset
equals the true boundary offset mod `s^k`):

| step | `κ*` | k=1 | k=2 | k=3 | k=4 | k=5 | k=6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.00 | 0.50 | 0.27 | 0.13 | 0.06 | 0.03 | 0.02 |
| 250 | 1.30 | 1.00 | 0.81 | 0.44 | 0.21 | 0.10 | 0.05 |
| 2 000 | 2.55 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.84 | 0.46 | 0.24 | 0.13 |
| 8 000 | 3.70 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.99 | 0.75 | 0.43 | 0.24 |
| 24 000 | 4.55 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.86 | 0.54 | 0.30 |
| 64 000 | 4.90 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.90 | 0.63 | 0.36 |
| chance | | 0.50 | 0.25 | 0.125 | 0.062 | 0.031 | 0.016 |
| **observer k's own ceiling** | | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.989 | 0.939 | 0.725 |

The ceiling row is observer `k`'s own posterior over the phase mod `s^k` at window positions
32–64 (`flat_predictive(..., return_phase=True)`), i.e. whether anything could find the boundary
from the window. It could, at every `k`. So the model's entropy carries the period, the frontier
switches on one level at a time in step with `κ*`, and the shortfall at `k = 5, 6` is the model's:
it reaches 100% of the ceiling through `k = 3`, 91% at `k = 4`, 67% at `k = 5`, 50% at `k = 6`.
(A per-window "dominant period" statistic needs several samples per offset and is only resolvable
up to `k = 4` in a 64-token window; the offset-accuracy numbers above have no such limit.)

**B. Where the residual lives.** The first pass compared the model's residual `KL(p_L‖q)` by leaf
level against the rung-to-rung news `KL(p_{k+1}‖p_k)`, which spikes at boundaries (by 5–25× over
its neighbours), and read the model's residual — spread over levels 0–2 — as "not shaped like a
missing rung". **That was the wrong comparison object.** Against the fitted observer's *own*
distance from truth, `KL(p_L‖p_κ*)` by leaf level, the two residuals have the same level-shape at
every checkpoint: a coarse observer discards the position-specific root prior and all
cross-subtree dependence, so its error is spread over every position inside its subtrees, not
concentrated at boundaries, exactly like the model's.

| step | `κ*` | `KL(p_L‖q)` | `KL(p_L‖p_κ*)` | **fitted observer's share of the model's residual** | L1 distance between the two level-share vectors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 250 | 1.30 | 0.541 | 0.429 | 0.79 | 0.084 |
| 1 000 | 2.20 | 0.272 | 0.197 | 0.72 | 0.067 |
| 2 000 | 2.55 | 0.202 | 0.142 | 0.70 | 0.072 |
| 4 000 | 2.85 | 0.130 | 0.111 | 0.86 | 0.084 |
| 8 000 | 3.70 | 0.085 | 0.044 | 0.52 | 0.075 |
| 16 000 | 4.40 | 0.054 | 0.017 | 0.32 | 0.062 |
| 24 000 | 4.55 | 0.041 | 0.013 | 0.32 | 0.065 |
| 64 000 | 4.90 | 0.017 | 0.007 | 0.40 | 0.069 |

What changes over training is the amount, not the shape. The fitted observer accounts for 70–89%
of the model's residual through `κ* ≤ 2.9` and 32–40% from `κ* ≥ 4.4`; the transition is between
steps 4k and 16k, the same stretch over which Q1's ratio crosses from 0.55 to 0.70. Per level
there is a diagonal: the accounting is best at leaf level `≈ κ*` (0.96 at level 1 when `κ* = 1.3`;
0.92–0.99 at level 2 when `κ* = 1.8–2.55`; 0.93 at level 4 when `κ* = 3.8`) and worst at leaf
levels 5–6 at every checkpoint after the first (0.14–0.60). The model's excess at root-adjacent
positions is the part no member of the family explains.

> **"The model is observer `κ*` plus approximation error" is a good description while the model
> is coarse, and the coarse part of the residual falls from about four-fifths to about a third as
> the model converges. The residual's shape is a coarse observer's throughout.**

## Q3 — the model's predictive as a null for scoring candidate units

Bayesian model comparison with the model as the reference. Candidates are adjacent pairs of
depth-`j` constituents `(A, B)` in held-out windows, enumerated with the oracle's parse and split by
the grammar into **true** (the two children of one depth-`(j+1)` node) and **chance** (straddling a
depth-`(j+1)` boundary). Token-span statistics die past `j = 2`, so the candidate is defined at the
feature level and its likelihood over `B`'s tokens is closed exactly:
`P_cand(B_tok | f_A) = Σ_f P̂(f | f_A, parity) · P_grammar(B_tok | f)`, with `P̂` a 16×16 table per
`(j, parity)` from a disjoint 200k-sequence corpus (what a bracketing-induction procedure that knows
depth-`j` boundaries but not depth-`(j+1)` ones would estimate for each competing bracketing) and
`P_grammar` an exact upward pass. Score per occurrence:
`Δ = −log q(B_tok | prefix) + log P_cand(B_tok | f_A)`, positive when the candidate explains `B`
better than the null did. Baselines: the same `Δ` with the exact observer `k` as the null, and
model-free PMI on the feature table. Event counts 114,688 / 55,314 / 25,598 / 8,678 / 241 for
`j = 1…5` (a `j = 5` pair spans the whole window, so only 4 of 64 phases admit one).

**The baselines, which set what "separates" means** (model-independent, constant over training):

| j | AUC PMI | AUC candidate gain | obs `k = j` as null | obs `k = j+1` as null | obs `k = 0` as null |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.922 | 0.906 | **0.890** | 0.467 | 0.805 |
| 2 | 0.952 | 0.943 | **0.939** | 0.513 | 0.768 |
| 3 | 0.936 | 0.918 | **0.891** | 0.533 | 0.687 |
| 4 | 0.958 | 0.939 | **0.901** | 0.550 | 0.642 |
| 5 | 0.933 | 0.925 | **0.879** | 0.537 | 0.605 |

The exact-observer null peaks at `k = j` and collapses to ~0.52 for every `k ≥ j+1` — a null that
has absorbed level `j+1` pays less on a true unit's second constituent by exactly the amount the
candidate gains, and the score cancels. That is absorption as a near-theorem of the design.

**The model as the null**, AUC(true vs chance):

| step | `κ*` | j=1 | j=2 | j=3 | j=4 | j=5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.00 | **0.807** | 0.759 | 0.666 | 0.628 | 0.577 |
| 250 | 1.30 | 0.766 | **0.805** | 0.716 | 0.664 | 0.599 |
| 1 000 | 2.20 | 0.557 | 0.801 | **0.766** | 0.706 | 0.587 |
| 2 000 | 2.55 | 0.530 | 0.672 | 0.765 | **0.720** | 0.670 |
| 8 000 | 3.70 | 0.531 | 0.551 | 0.622 | 0.693 | 0.669 |
| 24 000 | 4.55 | 0.536 | 0.531 | 0.575 | 0.653 | 0.637 |
| 64 000 | 4.90 | 0.544 | 0.529 | 0.531 | 0.598 | 0.671 |

Peaks at `κ* ≈ j − 1` (j=1 at 0.00, j=2 at 1.30, j=3 at 2.20, j=4 at 2.55; j=5 does not localise,
0.67–0.71 over a wide range at n≈120 per class). Peak values 0.81 / 0.81 / 0.77 / 0.72 decline
with `j` and never reach the `k = j` observer (0.88–0.94) or PMI (0.92–0.96). **The nats a true
unit still buys against the model** (`Δ / 2^j`, per token) fall monotonically and cross zero level
by level in order — `j = 1` at step 2000, `j = 2` at 16000, `j = 3–5` still positive at 64k
(+0.014 / +0.038 / +0.052). The confound is visible and works against the effect: `−log q(B)` alone
separates the classes *below* 0.5 at 64k (0.21–0.45 for `j = 1…5`), since the trained model pays
less on a second child than on a first, so the separation above is achieved despite it.

> **The model's own predictive adds no discriminative power over model-free count statistics for
> "is this a unit"; it degrades them. What it carries is which levels are still news to the model,
> and that read climbs the grammar in order with `κ*`.**

## Q4a — tonic: the missing oracle control

The parent's 2b population-matched pairs, kept bit-for-bit (same exact cells, same
nearest-neighbour matching on the *model's* surprisal, same seed and caliper 0.1); only the
readout is swapped for observer `k`'s running surprisal over the four tokens before the event.

| step | pairs | guard | **model** | obs 3 | obs 4 | obs 5 | **obs 6 (truth)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2603 | 0.500 | 0.503 | 0.598 | 0.659 | 0.731 | **0.734** |
| 2 000 | 1518 | 0.500 | 0.546 | 0.594 | 0.691 | 0.797 | 0.801 |
| 8 000 | 1162 | 0.500 | 0.643 | 0.600 | 0.698 | 0.832 | 0.838 |
| 24 000 | 859 | 0.500 | 0.696 | 0.581 | 0.686 | 0.854 | 0.860 |
| 64 000 | 605 | 0.501 | **0.754** | 0.559 | 0.657 | 0.873 | **0.878** |

The model's 0.754 reproduces the parent exactly. The exact observer reads 0.734 on the random-init
checkpoint's pairs and is above the model at every checkpoint. On the same shrinking pair
population the oracle's readout rises +0.144 where the model's rises +0.251, so roughly 57% of the
model's climb is the population changing under it. Only observers at `k ≥ 5` beat the model at
64k; observers at `k = 3–4` are worse than it.

> **The tonic signal is primarily a property of the stimulus: any coherent observer's running
> surprisal over the edited stretch is elevated, more than the model's.**

## Q4b — entropy direction: the two explanations come apart, and what the forecast moves toward

Same-prefix twins reconstructed exactly (caliper 0.3, `swap65k`, seed 0; the model's own `H_next`
AUC comes out at 0.449 at 64k, matching the parent). Paired win rate (> 0.5 = *less* confident
after the violation), 1200 pairs per checkpoint, against observer `k` **with** `noise_eps = 0.01`:

| step | **model** | obs 2+ε | obs 3+ε | obs 4+ε | obs 5+ε | obs 6+ε |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.479 | 0.527 | 0.630 | 0.756 | 0.865 | 0.854 |
| 2 000 | 0.398 | 0.439 | 0.527 | 0.726 | 0.877 | 0.869 |
| 8 000 | 0.410 | 0.414 | 0.449 | 0.637 | 0.847 | 0.835 |
| 24 000 | 0.407 | 0.399 | 0.387 | 0.570 | 0.813 | 0.810 |
| 64 000 | **0.433** | 0.416 | 0.369 | 0.489 | **0.771** | **0.771** |

Split by the violation's `k*` at 64k (n = 98 / 372 / 654 for `k* = 3/4/5`):

| reader | k*=3 | k*=4 | k*=5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| model | 0.449 | 0.465 | 0.417 |
| obs 3+ε | **0.612** | 0.300 | 0.347 |
| obs 4+ε | 0.612 | **0.772** | 0.318 |
| obs 5+ε | 0.592 | 0.747 | **0.849** |

An ε-noise observer's sign is set by whether it can see the violation: at `k ≥ k*` the token is
impossible under its grammar, only the ε term keeps the posterior defined, and it widens
(0.73–0.85); at `k < k*` the token is rare-but-legal evidence and the posterior sharpens
(0.30–0.42). The model shows the `k < k*` sign at every `k*`. The unmatched output-level
persistence says the same in nats: at the event, `dH` is +0.61 / +0.60 / +0.52 for the ε-observers
that see a `k* = 3/4/5` violation, ≈ 0 for those that do not, and +0.125 / +0.061 / +0.017 for
the model; on legal-but-rare edits model and observers agree (+0.053 vs +0.065–0.081).

**Both candidate explanations are ruled out.** Not "no noise model": every observer in the table has
one. Not "a coarser observer at the fitted altitude": at `k = 5 = κ*` the ε-observer widens (+0.52
nats, 0.77) where the model sharpens (+0.02, 0.42). And no member of the family combines the
model's sign with the model's detection (Part 2a: AUC 0.985 at `k* = 3`, 0.923 at `k* = 4`) — the
member with the model's entropy response cannot detect the violation at all.

**What the post-violation forecast moves toward.** `KL(q_next ‖ p_{k,next})` at `t_v + 1`, ε family
(a clean observer with `k ≥ k*` has no posterior after the violating token — defined on
0.97 / 0.88 / 0.57 / 0.02 / 0.00 of pairs for `k = 2…6` — and where defined its KL is dominated by
support mismatch, 2.5–160 nats). Clean-trained model at 64k, 500 scored pairs:

| | k*=3 (n=47) | k*=4 (n=152) | k*=5 (n=274) |
|---|---|---|---|
| after violation, obs k=2 | **0.182** | 0.293 | 0.296 |
| obs k=3 | 1.865 | **0.205** | 0.137 |
| obs k=4 | 2.062 | 1.539 | **0.103** |
| obs k=5 | 2.183 | 1.540 | 1.450 |
| obs k=6 | 2.184 | 1.536 | 1.413 |
| **argmin k, after violation** | **2** | **3** | **4** |
| argmin k, after the legal twin | 2 | 4 | 4 |

After an illegal token the model's next forecast is closest to the ε-noise observer at exactly
`k* − 1`, the finest observer for which the token it just saw was still legal, with an
order-of-magnitude cliff at `k = k*`. After the matched legal twin the same forecasts sit at
argmin `k ≈ 4` with no cliff. The ε-trained model (Q5) shows the same rule in its well-powered
cells (argmin 3 at `k* = 4`, n=141; 4 at `k* = 5`, n=208; its `k* ≤ 3` cells are flat across `k`
and their argmins are noise). The twin-side argmin of ≈ 4 sits below the `κ* ≈ 4.9` fitted on
clean windows; this is a selected population (edited windows, one position, pairs chosen by
surprisal matching), so the load-bearing comparison is violation vs twin within it — a shift of
one to two rungs down.

> **The model does not treat an illegal token as evidence that its reading is wrong. It falls
> back to the finest reading under which the token was possible, and under that reading the token
> is ordinary informative evidence — which is why its entropy goes down where a noise-aware
> Bayesian's goes up. The state registers the violation (Part 2c); the output reinterprets.**

## Q5 — a noise-trained trajectory

[`train_noisy.py`](train_noisy.py): the parent's recipe with every token independently replaced by
a uniform draw with probability `ε = 0.01`, applied before the `(x, y)` split so the model predicts
the corrupted token — exactly what the ε-noise observer's predictive is over (realised flip rate
0.0100; `eps_train = 0` is bit-identical to the parent's trajectory). Fit against 14 observers.

| trajectory | `min_κ KL(p_κ‖q)` on clean windows | `min_κ KL(p_κ^ε‖q)` | `κ*` | winner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| clean-trained, 64k | **0.0138** | 0.0441 | 4.90 | clean |
| ε-trained, 64k | 0.0226 | **0.0129** | 4.85 | ε |

Exact mirror image; the ε-trained model prefers the ε family at every checkpoint from 250 on, and
its altitude is unaffected (`κ* = 4.85` vs 4.90). The gap is family-relative: on its own training
distribution the ε-trained model reads `CE − H(q) = −0.002` against `p_L^ε` and `−0.061` against
the clean `p_L` (the identity holds against the distribution the model was trained on and is off
by 0.06 nats against a neighbouring one). A clean observer is undefined on 24% of positions of a
corrupted window; `dual_ladder` reports `defined_frac` rather than returning NaN.

The same-prefix readouts on the ε-trained model at 64k, clean-trained in brackets: 2c forecast
after the token 0.852 (0.847), state 0.904 (0.840); 2d graded legal-vs-legal 0.719 (0.669);
**2e `H_next` after a violation 0.467 / 0.440 (0.449 / 0.433)** — the sign does not change, at this
or any checkpoint (paired 0.41–0.48 across the trajectory), while the ε-observer at `k = 5` on the
same pairs reads 0.715.

> **Training on exactly the corruption the ε-observer models puts the model in that observer's
> family by the KL fit and leaves its post-violation entropy response pointing the wrong way.
> The phasic detection is if anything stronger, and the graded response keeps the normative sign,
> so the model is not globally insensitive; off-grammar input specifically makes it commit.**

## What this establishes, and what it does not

**Establishes** (one grammar, one architecture, the parent's trajectory plus one ε-trained twin):

- The parent's self-calibration headline is the temperature-direction stationarity condition of
  the loss. Its "which observer" headline stands as an altitude, best read continuously.
- The coarse-observer family describes the model well while it is coarse and less well as it
  converges: the fitted observer's share of the residual falls from ~80% to ~35% between
  `κ* ≈ 2.9` and `κ* ≈ 4.4`, with the residual's level-shape a coarse observer's throughout.
- The model's constituent boundaries are recoverable from its entropy profile alone, at the
  observer's own ceiling through `k = 3` and partially above; the frontier switches on one level
  at a time with `κ*`.
- Used as a null, the model's predictive is level-selective — it prices candidates one rung above
  its altitude and cancels once a level is absorbed — and is dominated by model-free count
  statistics for separating true units from chance neighbours.
- The parent's tonic result is a stimulus property.
- After a violation, the model's forecast is the noise-aware observer's at `k* − 1`. Neither a
  missing noise model nor coarseness explains the entropy sign, and noise training does not
  change it.

**Does not establish:**

- Anything about a model that stalls. Every late-training statement here is about a model that
  climbed to the top of its grammar; whether a converged model's residual at a rung NTP cannot
  learn (e.g. `m = 8` at this depth) stays coarse-observer-shaped, or how its share behaves, is
  untested. The residual-share instrument is the tool for that.
- Whether the fallback rule survives higher noise. At `ε = 0.01` the loss cost of dropping a rung
  instead of attributing the token to noise is roughly half a nat on 1% of positions, below the
  model's approximation error to its family, so there is little gradient pressure either way; a
  noise-dose sweep is the direct test.
- What a model overtrained on a collapsed distribution looks like under this instrument. Every
  internal measure here — calibration, family membership, entropy — is relative to the training
  distribution, so a coherent Bayesian about the wrong world would read as healthy; the observer
  fit would show its implied world drifting from the true grammar. The frozen-corpus checkpoints
  in [`../../practice/reread/lm/`](../../practice/reread/lm/README.md) are an existing venue
  (that node's finding 5 is the same state-versus-output dissociation by another route).
- Generality of Q3 beyond oracle-enumerated candidates: the true and chance populations differ
  intrinsically in tree position (second child vs first), which Q3's confound row makes visible.
- Transfer off `v16 s2 L6 m4`, off this architecture, or to natural language.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd experiments
# Q1–Q3: CPU passes over the parent's per-checkpoint *_calibration.npz arrays (no GPU)
modal run -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.identity::identity_sweep \
    --traj-dir /data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/traj_a1_s42
modal run -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.frontier::phase_identifiability          # observer ceilings (GPU, once)
modal run -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.frontier::frontier_sweep \
    --traj-dir /data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/traj_a1_s42
modal run -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.frontier::residual_sweep \
    --traj-dir /data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/traj_a1_s42              # Q2 B, per checkpoint
modal run -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.units::units_sweep \
    --traj-dir /data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/traj_a1_s42

# Q4: the two controls (observer caches once, then per-checkpoint sweeps)
modal run --detach -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.controls::tonic_sweep \
    --traj-dir /data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/traj_a1_s42 --stim-tag a1
modal run --detach -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.controls::observer_cache_sweep --stim-tag a1
modal run --detach -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.controls::entropy_direction_sweep \
    --traj-dir /data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/traj_a1_s42 --stim-tag swap65k
modal run -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.controls::persistence_at_k \
    --traj-dir /data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/traj_a1_s42 --stim-tag a1
modal run --detach -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.whither::whither_sweep \
    --ckpts /data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/traj_a1_s42/step064000.pt,/data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/traj_eps01_s42/step064000.pt

# Q5: the ε-trained trajectory (~55 min on an L4), both ladders, and the same-prefix readouts
modal run --detach -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.train_noisy::train_noisy --tag eps01_s42
modal run --detach -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.dual_ladder::ladder_cache_sweep
modal run --detach -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.dual_ladder::dual_sweep \
    --traj-dir /data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/traj_eps01_s42 --ws noisy0.01
modal run --detach -m rhm.logit_reading.phasic::phasic_sweep \
    --traj-dir /data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/traj_eps01_s42 --stim-tag swap65k --caliper 0.3
modal run --detach -m rhm.logit_reading.phasic::gradient_sweep \
    --traj-dir /data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/traj_eps01_s42 --stim-tag swap65k

# tables and figures (local, reads the JSONs pulled off the volume)
python -m rhm.logit_reading.altitude.analyze <dir> --figs rhm/logit_reading/altitude/figs
```

Results land on the `rhm-scaling-data` volume (**`chromatic` workspace**) under
`/data/v16_s2_L6_m4_distinct/logit_reading/`: `traj_a1_s42/altitude_{identity,frontier,residual,units,persistence_a1}.json`,
`altitude_phase_identifiability.json`, `traj_a1_s42/step*_{tonic_a1,entdir_swap65k,dual_clean}.json`,
`obs_a1_k{2..6}_eps0.01.npz`, `ladder_d{0.0,0.01}_o{0.0,0.01}.npz`, the new trajectory `traj_eps01_s42/`
(13 checkpoints and `step*_{dual_clean,dual_noisy0.01,phasic_swap65k_cal0.3,gradient_swap65k,entdir_swap65k}.json`),
and `traj_{a1,eps01}_s42/step064000_whither_swap65k.json`.

## Gotchas worth not rediscovering

- **`CE − H(q)` is a derivative, not a measurement.** Any "the model predicts its own loss" claim on
  a softmax model needs a comparison the temperature direction cannot zero (per-class gaps are
  the natural one, and here they are all within ±0.015).
- **Compare a model's residual against the fitted observer's residual, not against rung-to-rung
  news.** The news spikes at boundaries; a coarse observer's error does not. The first reading of
  Q2 B got this wrong.
- **Log-linear interpolation between nested-support observers is discontinuous at `λ = 0`.** Use
  the convex family.
- **The clean observer family is undefined after an off-grammar token** (and on 24% of positions
  of an ε-corrupted window). Any post-violation comparison needs the ε family; report
  `defined_frac`, never drop the NaNs silently.
- **Token-span statistics for candidate units die past `j = 2`.** Define candidates at the feature
  level with the exact realisation term and keep the two model-free baselines beside every
  model-as-null number, or a failure above the frontier cannot be attributed.
- **The parent's per-checkpoint `*_calibration.npz` arrays make Q1–Q3 free.** All 13 checkpoints
  share one window set and one set of observer predictives; anything that is a function of
  `(q, p_k, windows, phase)` needs no GPU.
